verification_basis: official public internet sources; confidence is source-authority confidence, not parcel numeric confidence

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - point density considered in the LiDAR programme
verified_facts: EA states average point density depends on target surface-model resolution: at least 1 ppsqm for 1m DSM, 4 ppsqm for 50cm and 16 ppsqm for 25cm.
EA explicitly distinguishes irregular point-cloud density from raster resolution and notes DTM ground-return density can be lower under vegetation.
semantic_limits: Point density must not be converted into an equivalent DTM accuracy claim.
Point-cloud density does not replace the final edited DTM values.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - opening and using downloaded LiDAR files
verified_facts: EA states LiDAR is a technical dataset requiring GIS software for use.
The FAQ distinguishes viewing imagery/preview from working with the underlying elevation data.
semantic_limits: Software display or rendering is not an independent terrain observation.
Numeric values must be preserved through any GIS processing step.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - downloading large areas of LiDAR data
verified_facts: EA states portal LiDAR downloads are supplied in 5km by 5km tiles and large-area bulk requests are not handled by the standard portal workflow.
semantic_limits: Download packaging limits do not change source measurement semantics.
Missing local download packaging must not be interpreted as no terrain data.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - accessing the current LiDAR capture programme
verified_facts: EA provides a capture-programme application covering current forward-looking winter capture and previous seasons.
semantic_limits: Capture-programme presence is planning/freshness evidence only until matched to a parcel-specific survey record.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - LiDAR data metadata
verified_facts: EA states index catalogues can be downloaded for all LiDAR products and include collection-time information.
semantic_limits: Catalogue availability is not contributing-survey proof without exact spatial feature matching.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - where to view LiDAR data
verified_facts: EA says WMS Preview provides an image of Composite LiDAR data or coverage extents.
EA explicitly states the preview image cannot be queried.
semantic_limits: WMS preview pixels must never be used as native DTM numeric samples.
Coverage preview is visual discovery only.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - where to view and download metadata for all LiDAR products
verified_facts: EA directs users to the LiDAR Capture Programme for metadata and coverage maps and states its survey catalogue covers England.
semantic_limits: A coverage map is not a sampled terrain surface.
No listed survey must remain no-data/unknown rather than zero elevation.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - ASCII to GeoTIFFs
verified_facts: EA moved Composite DTM delivery from ASCII to GeoTIFF and supplies 1m/2m products in 5km tiles with elevation values in metres.
EA states GeoTIFF enables web services such as image services and WCS.
semantic_limits: Format migration must not change terrain values, CRS or vertical datum semantics.
A web-service representation is not automatically a native sample.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - Environment Agency data coverage
verified_facts: EA directs users to the index catalogue to establish which LiDAR products are available in each grid square.
semantic_limits: Grid-square coverage does not identify the exact contributing composite survey at a parcel.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - LiDAR data survey schedule
verified_facts: EA publishes a survey programme and directs users to capture-programme information for current and planned progress.
semantic_limits: Planned survey scheduling is not evidence that a parcel was actually captured or used in the composite.

candidates.name: Other HM Land Registry plan-related services and guides (PG40 supplement 6)
verified_facts: HMLR explains the index map as an OS-based index of registered titles and pending first-registration applications.
Search of the index map and official-copy services are separate; illustrative plans show relative title locations rather than exact title extents.
semantic_limits: Index-map/illustrative plan output must not be promoted to exact legal boundary geometry.

candidates.name: How to read a title plan
verified_facts: HMLR says the title plan supports the register and uses OS mapping to show a visual indication of registered land.
HMLR explicitly warns red edging cannot be treated as the exact legal boundary and measurements scaled from the plan should not be relied on to locate the legal line.
semantic_limits: Title-plan red edging is legal/planimetric context, not elevation measurement evidence.

candidates.name: Practice guide 10: official search of the index map
verified_facts: The current guide states index-map plans issued with SIM results are illustrative only and do not define the extent of an individual title.
It states official title-plan copies carry a general-boundary warning and scaled measurements may not match ground measurements.
semantic_limits: SIM plans must not be reused as exact parcel geometry.
Index-map identification must be followed by title-specific evidence where exact extent matters.

candidates.name: Get information about property and land - Search the index map
verified_facts: HMLR describes the index map as a way to find title numbers and confirm whether land is registered.
Address, clearly identifying plan or OS map reference may be used to identify the search area.
semantic_limits: Title-number discovery is identification evidence only and does not prove exact polygon geometry or height values.

candidates.name: HM Land Registry portal - how to request official copies
verified_facts: HMLR portal workflow can order official copies of a register, title plan and referenced documents by title number/property details.
semantic_limits: Retrieval workflow is documentary provenance, not automatic exact-boundary evidence.

candidates.name: Finding information held by HM Land Registry
verified_facts: HMLR distinguishes standard search/download results from official copies required for legal proof in some contexts.
semantic_limits: Document status affects evidential use, not terrain measurement accuracy.

candidates.name: Official copies of register or plan: registration (OC1)
verified_facts: OC1 is the official-copy route for register/title plan documents.
GOV.UK notes an official title plan will likely show general rather than exact boundaries.
semantic_limits: Official-copy status does not convert a general boundary into a determined exact boundary.

candidates.name: HM Land Registry Information Services guidance
verified_facts: The HMLR information-services hub routes users to index-map, official-copy and property-description services and the corresponding practice guides.
semantic_limits: Service routing is provenance/discovery evidence only, not parcel geometry or elevation evidence.
